sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction (Purpose, Scope, Definitions)
sections.body:
**Purpose:**
This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines the technical requirements for the Hospital EMR Patient Management System (Patient Portal). The document serves as a baseline for the design, implementation, and verification of the system.

**Scope:**
This SRS covers the functional and non-functional requirements for the Patient Portal, focusing on patient-facing interactions with the Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system. 

*Note: The source document excerpt is highly condensed ("Hospital EMR patient management system"). Specific functional modules (e.g., appointment scheduling, lab results viewing, secure messaging) are not explicitly detailed in the source. These are treated as open items requiring stakeholder input to define exact functional boundaries.*

**Definitions:**
- **EMR:** Electronic Medical Record.
- **PHI:** Protected Health Information.
- **HIPAA:** Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.
- **P95 Latency:** The 95th percentile of response times.

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body:
**System Context:**
The Patient Portal acts as a secure interface between patients and the Hospital EMR. It allows patients to access their health data, communicate with providers, and manage appointments.

**Architecture Overview:**
*Open Item:* The source document does not specify the architectural pattern (e.g., microservices, monolithic), database technology, or integration points with the core EMR. Stakeholder input is required to define the technical architecture.

**User Classes:**
- **Patient:** Primary user accessing their own health records.
- **Healthcare Provider:** Secondary user interacting via the portal (e.g., messaging).
- **System Administrator:** Manages user accounts and system configuration.

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: System shall support secure user authentication for patients and providers.
System shall allow patients to view their medical records stored in the EMR.
System shall provide a secure messaging interface between patients and providers.

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements
sections.body:
**Performance:**
- **NFR-001:** The system shall maintain a P95 latency of < 250ms for standard API requests, per healthcare domain benchmarks.

**Security & Compliance (HIPAA):**
- **NFR-002 (Encryption at Rest):** All Protected Health Information (PHI) stored in the database or file systems must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 or equivalent industry-standard encryption, per HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv).
- **NFR-003 (Audit Logging):** The system shall implement comprehensive audit logging for all access to PHI. Logs must record the user ID, timestamp, action performed, and data accessed. These logs must be tamper-evident and retained for a minimum of 6 years, per HIPAA §164.312(b) and §164.316(b)(2)(i).

**Reliability:**
- **NFR-004:** The system shall achieve 99.9% availability during business hours.

*Note: Specific reliability and availability metrics beyond the latency benchmark are not defined in the source document and are listed as open items for stakeholder confirmation.*

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements
sections.body:
**APIs:**
- **API-001:** The portal shall integrate with the core Hospital EMR via a secure RESTful API to retrieve patient data.
- *Open Item:* Specific API endpoints, data formats (JSON/XML), and authentication protocols (OAuth2, mTLS) are not defined in the source. Stakeholder input required.

**UI:**
- **UI-001:** The user interface shall be responsive and accessible, supporting WCAG 2.1 AA standards.

**Hardware:**
- *Open Item:* No specific hardware constraints are mentioned in the source document.

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body:
**Compliance Framework:**
- The system must comply with HIPAA Security and Privacy Rules.
- **Verification Method:** Compliance will be verified through security penetration testing, code review for encryption implementation, and audit log integrity checks.

**Constraints:**
- **C-001:** All data transmission must occur over TLS 1.2 or higher.
- **C-002:** The system must operate within the hospital's existing network infrastructure.

*Note: The source document is silent on specific technology stack constraints (e.g., Java, .NET, AWS/Azure). These are open items requiring stakeholder input.*
